title: Where Did Bats Come From? Scientists Point to Europe
summary:
Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly by flapping their wings. But where did the very first bats live? Scientists have argued about this for decades. Africa, Asia and North America have all been suggested as the birthplace.

Now a large international team says bats most likely began in Europe. The team included 137 researchers from 64 countries. They worked through a project called Bat1K, which aims to read the genomes of all living bat species. A genome is the full set of instructions, written in DNA, inside a living thing.

The scientists studied 103 bat genomes, including 42 new ones, covering all 21 recognized bat families. They also used evidence from 44 fossil bats. The study was published in the journal Nature.

The results suggest that bats first evolved in Europe in the late Paleocene, roughly 65 to 60 million years ago. Their descendants then moved into Africa. Later, different groups spread into the Americas, Asia and Australia. Those moves created the main kinds of bats we see around the world today.

The study also gives clues about bat abilities. A fossil bat called Vielasia sits on the oldest branch of the bat family tree. It suggests that echolocation, which means using sound to find your way and hunt in the dark, appeared close to the start of bat evolution. The evidence suggests that both flight and echolocation appeared before modern bat groups began to split apart.

Bats make up about one fifth of all living mammals. Scientists say the new family tree will help them learn how and where bats' special traits evolved.
why_it_matters: Knowing where and when bats began helps scientists understand how their special traits, such as flight and echolocation, developed.

questions.question: What special ability do bats have among mammals?
options: They can truly fly by flapping their wings
They can breathe underwater for hours
They can live only in cold places
They can run faster than all birds
questions.correct_answer: They can truly fly by flapping their wings

questions.question: Where does the new study say bats most likely began?
options: North America
Asia
Europe
Africa

questions.question: What is Bat1K?
options: A museum room that stores every bat fossil
A project that aims to read the genomes of all living bat species
A school contest about bats for young students
A zoo that keeps one thousand different kinds of bats
questions.correct_answer: A project that aims to read the genomes of all living bat species

options: Roughly 65 to 60 thousand years ago
Roughly 650 to 600 years ago
Roughly 65 to 60 million years ago
Roughly 6 to 5 million years ago

options: Bats first learned to fly only recently
Bats once lived only in deserts
Echolocation appeared close to the start of bat evolution
Bats used to hunt only in daylight

background_read: Paleocene is the name of a time in Earth's history that began after the dinosaurs died out. The late Paleocene is the later part of that time.
